title.en: Volume 1 Book of Later Liang 1: Taizu Annals 1
title.raw: 卷一 梁書1: 太祖本紀一 Volume 1 Book of Later Liang 1: Taizu Annals 1

sentences.zh: 太祖神武元聖孝皇帝，姓朱氏，諱晃，本名溫，宋州碭山人。

translations.literal: Taizu, the Divine Martial, Primordially Sagely, Filial Emperor, bore the surname Zhu; his taboo name was Huang; his original name was Wen; he was a native of Dangshan in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, styled the Divine Martial, Primordially Sagely, Filial Emperor, was of the Zhu clan; his taboo name was Huang, his birth name Wen, and he came from Dangshan in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 其先，舜司徒虎之後。

translations.literal: His ancestors were descendants of Hu, Minister of Works under Shun.
translations.idiomatic: His line traced back to Hu, Minister of Works in the age of Shun.

sentences.zh: 高祖黯，曾祖茂琳，祖信，父誠。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather Maolin; his grandfather Xin; his father Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Maolin, his grandfather Xin, and his father Cheng.

sentences.zh: 帝即誠之第三子，母曰文惠王皇后。

translations.literal: The Emperor was the third son of Cheng; his mother was called the Honored Queen of the Cultured and Gracious King.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was Cheng's third son; his mother was known as the queen of the Cultured and Gracious King.

sentences.zh: 《五代會要》：梁肅祖宣元皇帝諱黯，舜司徒虎四十二代孫；

translations.literal: The 《Wudai huiyao》 says: The Sagely Ancestor of Liang, the Emperor Xuan Yuan, taboo name An, was the forty-second-generation descendant of Hu, Minister of Works under Shun;
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that Liang's Sagely Ancestor, Emperor Xuan Yuan, taboo name An, was forty-second in descent from Shun's Minister of Works Hu;

sentences.zh: 開平元年七月，追尊宣元皇帝，廟號肅祖，葬興極陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Kaiping, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan Yuan, with temple name Sagely Ancestor, and buried at Xingji Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1.7 he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan Yuan, given the temple name Sagely Ancestor, and interred at Xingji Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 敬祖光獻皇帝諱茂琳，宣元皇帝長子，母曰宣僖皇后范氏；

translations.literal: The Revered Ancestor, the Emperor Guangxian, taboo name Maolin, eldest son of Emperor Xuan Yuan, mother called the Honored Empress Xuanxi of the Fan clan;
translations.idiomatic: The Revered Ancestor, Emperor Guangxian, taboo Maolin, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan Yuan; his mother was Honored Empress Xuanxi, née Fan;

sentences.zh: 開平元年七月，追尊光獻皇帝，廟號敬祖，葬永安陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Kaiping, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Guangxian, with temple name Revered Ancestor, and buried at Yong'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1.7 he was posthumously honored as Emperor Guangxian, given the temple name Revered Ancestor, and buried at Yong'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 憲祖昭武皇帝諱信，光獻皇帝長子，母曰光孝皇后楊氏；

translations.literal: The Exalted Ancestor, the Emperor Zhaowu, taboo name Xin, eldest son of Emperor Guangxian, mother called the Honored Empress Guangxiao of the Yang clan;
translations.idiomatic: The Exalted Ancestor, Emperor Zhaowu, taboo Xin, was the eldest son of Emperor Guangxian; his mother was Honored Empress Guangxiao, née Yang;

sentences.zh: 開平元年七月，追尊昭武皇帝，廟號憲祖，葬光天陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Kaiping, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaowu, with temple name Exalted Ancestor, and buried at Guangtian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1.7 he was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaowu, given the temple name Exalted Ancestor, and buried at Guangtian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 烈祖文穆皇帝諱誠，昭武皇帝長子，母曰昭懿皇后劉氏；

translations.literal: The August Ancestor, the Emperor Wenmu, taboo name Cheng, eldest son of Emperor Zhaowu, mother called the Honored Empress Zhaoyi of the Liu clan;
translations.idiomatic: The August Ancestor, Emperor Wenmu, taboo Cheng, was the eldest son of Emperor Zhaowu; his mother was Honored Empress Zhaoyi, née Liu;

sentences.zh: 開平元年七月，追尊文穆皇帝，廟號烈祖，葬咸寧陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Kaiping, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wenmu, with temple name August Ancestor, and buried at Xianning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1.7 he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wenmu, given the temple name August Ancestor, and buried at Xianning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 以唐大中六年歲在壬申，十月二十一日夜，生於碭山縣午溝裏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Dazhong era of Tang, the year in renshen, on the night of the twenty-first day of the tenth month, he was born in Wugou village, Dangshan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the night of the twenty-first day of the tenth month of Dazhong 6 (852), in Wugou village, Dangshan County.

sentences.zh: 是夕，所居廬舍之上有赤氣上騰。

translations.literal: That evening, above the thatched dwelling where they lived, red vapor rose upward.
translations.idiomatic: That night red vapor rose above the family's hut.

sentences.zh: 里人望之，皆驚奔而來，曰：「朱家火發矣！

translations.literal: The villagers who saw it all ran in alarm, saying, "The Zhu household is on fire!
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors who saw it came running in alarm, crying, "The Zhu house is burning!

sentences.zh: 」及至，則廬舍儼然。

translations.literal: " When they arrived, the dwelling stood intact as before.
translations.idiomatic: " But when they reached the spot the hut stood untouched.

sentences.zh: 既入，鄰人以誕孩告，眾鹹異之。

translations.literal: Once inside, neighbors reported that a child had been born; all regarded it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Inside they learned a child had been born, and everyone took it for an omen.

sentences.zh: 昆仲三人，俱未冠而孤，母攜養寄于蕭縣人劉崇之家。

translations.literal: The three brothers, all still without caps and orphaned, were brought up by their mother, who lodged them with Liu Chong of Xiao County.
translations.idiomatic: All three brothers lost their father before coming of age; their mother raised them as guests in the home of Liu Chong of Xiao County.

sentences.zh: 帝既壯，不事生業，以雄勇自負，里人多厭之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had grown strong, he would not engage in livelihood; he prided himself on fierce courage, and many in the village disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he shunned honest work, swaggered in his strength, and was widely disliked in the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 崇以其慵惰，每加譴杖。

translations.literal: Chong, because of his laziness, often rebuked and beat him with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Chong beat him often for idleness.

sentences.zh: 唯崇母自幼憐之，親為櫛發，嘗誡家人曰：「朱三非常人也，汝輩當善待之。

translations.literal: Only Chong's mother had pitied him from childhood, personally combing his hair, and once warned the household, saying, "Zhu the Third is no ordinary man; you should treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chong's mother had favored him since boyhood, combing his hair herself, and once told the family, "Zhu the Third is no ordinary man—you must treat him kindly.

sentences.zh: 」家人問其故，答曰：「我嘗見其熟寐之次，化為一赤蛇。

translations.literal: " The family asked the reason; she answered, "I once saw him in deep sleep transform into a red serpent.
translations.idiomatic: " When they asked why, she said, "Once, while he slept soundly, I saw him become a red serpent.

sentences.zh: 」然眾亦未之信也。

translations.literal: " Yet the crowd still did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: " Still, no one quite believed her.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，巢以帝為同州防禦使，使自攻取。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Chao appointed the Emperor Defender of Tong Prefecture and ordered him to take it himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year Huang Chao made him defender of Tongzhou and told him to seize the post on his own.

sentences.zh: 帝乃自丹州南行，以擊左馮翊，拔之，遂據其郡。

translations.literal: The Emperor then marched south from Dan Prefecture to strike Zuofengyi, captured it, and thereupon held that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south from Danzhou, stormed Zuofengyi, and held the commandery.

sentences.zh: 時河中節度使王重榮屯兵數萬，糾合諸侯，以圖興復。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Chongrong, military governor of Hezhong, encamped tens of thousands of troops and rallied the feudatories to plan restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, governor of Hezhong, had tens of thousands in the field and was rallying the lords to restore the Tang.

sentences.zh: 帝時與之鄰封，屢為重榮所敗，遂請濟師於巢。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then on a neighboring border and was repeatedly defeated by Chongrong; he therefore requested reinforcements from Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Bordering Chongrong's territory, he suffered repeated defeats and begged Chao for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 表章十上，為偽左軍使孟楷所蔽，不達。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials ten times, but they were concealed by the false Left Army Commissioner Meng Kai and did not get through.
translations.idiomatic: He sent ten memorials, but Meng Kai, the rebel Left Army commissioner, blocked every one.

sentences.zh: 又聞巢軍勢蹙，諸校離心，帝知其必敗。

translations.literal: He also heard that Chao's army was pressed and that the officers were losing heart; the Emperor knew he was bound to fail.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Chao's forces were failing and his officers wavering, he saw defeat coming.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝遂與左右定計，斬偽監軍使嚴實，舉郡降于重榮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor then settled plans with his close attendants, beheaded the false military inspector Yan Shi, and surrendered the commandery to Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he plotted with his intimates, executed the rebel inspector Yan Shi, and surrendered his commandery to Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 重榮即日飛章上奏。

translations.literal: Chongrong that same day sent a flying memorial to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong that day rushed a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，覽表而喜曰：「是天賜予也！

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; reading the memorial he rejoiced and said, "Heaven has given him to me!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong, then in Shu, read the report and exclaimed, "Heaven has sent him to me!

sentences.zh: 」乃詔授帝左金吾衛大將軍，充河中行營副招討使。

translations.literal: " He then issued an edict appointing the Emperor Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and making him deputy campaign commissioner of the Hezhong field army.
translations.idiomatic: " He appointed him Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and deputy campaign commissioner of the Hezhong field army.

sentences.zh: 仍賜名全忠。

translations.literal: He was also granted the name Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court also granted him the name Quanzhong—"wholly loyal."

sentences.zh: 自是率所部與河中兵士偕行，所向無不克捷。

translations.literal: From then on he led his troops together with the soldiers of Hezhong, and wherever they went there was nothing that did not meet with swift victory.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he fought beside the Hezhong army and won wherever he turned.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，僖宗制授帝宣武軍節度使，依前充河中行營副招討使，仍令候收復京闕，即得赴鎮。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Emperor Xizong by imperial order appointed the Emperor military governor of the Xuanwu army, continuing as before as deputy campaign commissioner of the Hezhong field army, and still ordered that once the capital passes were recovered he might proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year Xizong named him military governor of Xuanwu, kept him as Hezhong's deputy campaign commissioner, and told him to take up the post once the capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 四月，巢軍自藍關南走，帝與諸侯之師俱收長安，乃率部下一旅之眾，仗節東下。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Chao's army fled south through Languan Pass; the Emperor together with the armies of the feudatories recovered Chang'an, then led a detachment of his command east under his commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, as Chao fled south through Languan, he joined the allied armies in retaking Chang'an, then marched east at the head of a detachment.

sentences.zh: 七月丁卯，入于梁苑。

translations.literal: On dingmao day of the seventh month he entered Liang Park.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day in the seventh month he entered Liang Park.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝年三十有二。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was thirty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 時蔡州刺史秦宗權與黃巢餘孽合從肆虐，共圍陳州。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Zongquan, prefect of Cai Prefecture, joined with the remnants of Huang Chao to run riot together and jointly besieged Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture had joined Huang Chao's remnants in ravaging the countryside and was besieging Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，僖宗乃命帝為東北面都招討使。

translations.literal: After a long time, Emperor Xizong then ordered the Emperor to be Grand Campaign Commissioner of the Northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Only after long delay did Xizong name him grand campaign commissioner of the northeast.

sentences.zh: 時汴、宋連年阻饑，公私俱困，帑廩皆虛，外為大敵所攻，內則驕軍難制，交鋒接戰，日甚一日；

translations.literal: At that time Bian and Song had suffered famine year after year; public and private were alike distressed, the treasuries were empty, outside they were attacked by a great enemy, inside the arrogant troops were hard to control, and clashes in battle grew worse day by day;
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Song had suffered famine for years; treasuries were empty, a great enemy pressed from without, unruly troops within, and fighting grew fiercer by the day;

sentences.zh: 人皆危之，惟帝銳氣益振。

translations.literal: All men regarded the situation as perilous, but only the Emperor's keen spirit grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: others despaired, but his fighting spirit only rose.

sentences.zh: 是歲十二月，帝領兵于鹿邑，與巢眾相遇，縱兵擊之，斬首二千餘級，乃引兵入亳州，因是兼有譙郡之地。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year the Emperor led troops at Luyi, met Chao's horde, loosed his soldiers to strike them, and cut off more than two thousand heads; he then led his army into Bozhou and thereby also gained the territory of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month he met Chao's band at Luyi, routed them, and took more than two thousand heads; he then entered Bozhou and with it gained Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年春，帝與許州田從異諸軍同收瓦子寨，殺賊數萬眾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Emperor together with the armies of Tian Congyi of Xuzhou and others jointly recovered Wazi Stockade and killed tens of thousands of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he joined Tian Congyi of Xuzhou and others to take Wazi Stockade and kill tens of thousands of rebels.

sentences.zh: 是時，陳州四面，賊寨相望，驅擄編氓，殺以充食，號為「舂磨寨」。

translations.literal: At that time on all four sides of Chen Prefecture rebel stockades faced one another; they drove off and seized common folk, killing them for food, and called them "Pounding and Grinding Stockades."
translations.idiomatic: Rebel camps ringed Chenzhou on every side, dragging off civilians to kill for food in camps they called "Pounding and Grinding."

sentences.zh: 帝分兵翦撲，大小凡四十戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor divided his forces to cut them down; in large and small engagements there were forty battles in all.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to destroy them in forty engagements large and small.

sentences.zh: 四月丁巳，收西華寨，賊將黃鄴單騎奔陳。

translations.literal: On dingsi day of the fourth month he recovered Xihua Stockade; the rebel general Huang Ye fled alone on horseback to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day in the fourth month he took Xihua Stockade; the rebel Huang Ye fled alone into Chen.

sentences.zh: 帝乘勝追之，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: The Emperor pursued in victory, advancing with drums and shouts.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit with drums and shouts.

sentences.zh: 會黃巢遁去，遂入陳州，刺史趙犨迎于馬前。

translations.literal: Just then Huang Chao had slipped away, so he entered Chen Prefecture, and the prefect Zhao Chou welcomed him before his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had already fled; he entered Chenzhou, where Prefect Zhao Chou met him at his horse.

sentences.zh: 俄聞巢党尚在陳北故陽壘，帝遂徑歸大樑。

translations.literal: Soon he heard that Chao's partisans were still at the old Yang stockade north of Chen; the Emperor then went straight back to Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chao's men still held the old Yang camp north of the city, he marched straight back to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 是時，河東節度使李克用奉僖宗詔，統騎軍數千同謀破賊，與帝合勢于中牟北邀擊之，賊眾大敗于王滿渡，多束手來降。

translations.literal: At that time Li Keyong, military governor of Hedong, obeying Emperor Xizong's edict, commanded several thousand cavalry to join in breaking the bandits; he united his strength with the Emperor north of Zhongmou to intercept them, and the rebel horde suffered a great defeat at Wangman Ford; many came with bound hands to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Hedong, under imperial orders, brought thousands of horsemen to join him; north of Zhongmou they smashed the rebels at Wangman Ford, and many surrendered with hands bound.

sentences.zh: 時賊將霍存、葛從周、張歸厚、張歸霸皆匍匐于馬前，悉宥而納之，遂逐殘寇，東至於冤句。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel generals Huo Cun, Ge Congzhou, Zhang Guihou, and Zhang Guiba all prostrated themselves before his horse; he pardoned and enrolled them all, then pursued the remnant bandits east as far as Yuanju.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Huo Cun, Ge Congzhou, Zhang Guihou, and Zhang Guiba threw themselves before his horse; he spared them and enrolled them, then chased the survivors east to Yuanju.

sentences.zh: 五月甲戌，帝與晉軍振旅歸汴，館克用於上源驛。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day of the fifth month the Emperor together with the Jin army raised the banners and returned to Bian, lodging Keyong at Shangyuan Post.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the fifth month he returned to Bian with Keyong's army and lodged Keyong at Shangyuan Post.

sentences.zh: 既而備犒宴之禮，克用乘醉任氣，帝不平之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he prepared a feast with rewards; Keyong, drunk, gave free rein to his temper, and the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared a reward feast, but Keyong, drunk and overbearing, angered him.

sentences.zh: 是夜，命甲士圍而攻之。

translations.literal: That night he ordered armored soldiers to surround and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent armored men to surround and attack him.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雷電，克用因得於電光中逾垣遁去，惟殺其部下數百人而已。

translations.literal: Just then great rain and thunder and lightning came; Keyong therefore was able in a flash of lightning to leap the wall and escape, and only several hundred of his subordinates were killed.
translations.idiomatic: A thunderstorm broke; Keyong leapt the wall in a flash of lightning and escaped, though several hundred of his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 六月，陳人感解圍之惠，為帝建生祠堂於其郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the people of Chen, grateful for the favor of lifting the siege, built a living shrine to the Emperor in their commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the people of Chen, grateful for the relief of the siege, built him a living shrine in their prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，黃巢雖歿，而蔡州秦宗權繼為巨孽，有眾數萬，攻陷鄰郡，殺掠吏民，屠害之酷，更甚巢賊，帝患之。

translations.literal: That year, although Huang Chao had died, Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture succeeded him as a great scourge, with tens of thousands of men; he attacked and seized neighboring commanderies, killed and plundered officials and people, and his slaughter was more cruel than even Chao's bandits; the Emperor was troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huang Chao was dead, Qin Zongquan of Cai became an even greater scourge, with tens of thousands of men ravaging neighboring prefectures with cruelty worse than Chao's; the emperor brooded over him.

sentences.zh: 七月，遂與陳人共攻蔡賊于溵水，殺數千人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he then together with the people of Chen attacked the Cai bandits at Yinshui and killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he joined the Chenzhou men to strike Qin's men at Yinshui and kill several thousand.

sentences.zh: 九月己未，僖宗就加帝檢校司徒、同平章事，封沛郡侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: On jiwei day of the ninth month Emperor Xizong added to his titles the Emperor as Acting Minister of Works and Co-Rector of State, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pei commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day in the ninth month Xizong promoted him to acting Minister of Works and co-rector of state, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pei with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 二年春，蔡賊益熾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year the Cai bandits grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year the Cai rebels grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 時唐室微弱，諸道州兵不為王室所用，故宗權得以縱毒，連陷汝、洛、懷、孟、唐、鄧、許、鄭，圜幅數千里，殆絕人煙，惟宋、亳、滑、潁僅能閉壘而已。

translations.literal: At that time the Tang house was weak; the troops of the various circuits and prefectures were not used for the royal house, so Zongquan was able to run wild; he successively seized Ru, Luo, Huai, Meng, Tang, Deng, Xu, and Zheng, a circuit of several thousand li where human life nearly ceased, and only Song, Bo, Hua, and Ying could barely shut their walls.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang court was feeble and provincial armies served their own masters, so Zongquan ran unchecked through Ru, Luo, Huai, Meng, Tang, Deng, Xu, and Zheng—a wasteland thousands of li wide—while only Song, Bo, Hua, and Ying could still hold their walls.

sentences.zh: 帝累出兵與之交戰，然或勝或負，人甚危之。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly led troops out to fight them, yet sometimes he won and sometimes he lost, and men regarded the situation as very perilous.
translations.idiomatic: He fought them again and again with mixed success, and men grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 三月庚辰，僖宗降制就封帝為沛郡王。

translations.literal: On gengchen day of the third month Emperor Xizong by edict enfeoffed the Emperor as Prince of Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day in the third month Xizong enfeoffed him as Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 是月，僖宗移幸興元。

translations.literal: That month Emperor Xizong moved his residence to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xizong moved his court to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 五月，嗣襄王煴僭即帝位于長安，改元為建貞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the heir Prince of Xiang, Yun, presumptuously took the imperial throne at Chang'an and changed the era name to Jianzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the heir Prince of Xiang, Yun, usurped the throne at Chang'an and proclaimed the era Jianzhen.

sentences.zh: 遣使齎偽詔至汴，帝命焚之於庭。

translations.literal: He sent envoys bearing a false edict to Bian; the Emperor ordered it burned in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: When a forged edict reached Bian, he had it burned in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，襄王果敗。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Xiang was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Xiang was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 七月，蔡人逼許州，節度使鹿宴宏使來求救，帝遣葛從周等率師赴援。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the men of Cai pressed Xuzhou; the military governor Lu Yanhong sent to beg rescue; the Emperor dispatched Ge Congzhou and others to lead troops to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Cai forces besieged Xuzhou; Governor Lu Yanhong begged for aid, and he sent Ge Congzhou to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 師未至而城陷，宴宏為蔡賊所害。

translations.literal: The army had not yet arrived when the city fell, and Yanhong was killed by the Cai bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The relief army arrived too late; the city fell and Yanhong was killed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，滑州節度使安師儒以怠於軍政，為部下所殺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month An Shiru, military governor of Hua Prefecture, because he was slack in military affairs, was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month An Shiru of Huazhou, negligent in military affairs, was murdered by his own men.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，乃遣朱珍、李唐賓襲而取之，由是遂有滑台之地。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he sent Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin to strike and take it, and thereby gained the territory of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, he sent Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin to seize the province and thereby gained Huatai.

sentences.zh: 十二月，僖宗降制就加帝檢校太傅，改封吳興郡王，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Emperor Xizong by edict added to his titles the Emperor as Acting Grand Tutor, changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Wuxing commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xizong promoted him to acting Grand Tutor and changed his title to Prince of Wuxing with a three-thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鄭州為蔡賊所陷，刺史李璠單騎來奔，帝宥而納之，以為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: That year Zheng Prefecture was seized by the Cai bandits; the prefect Li Fan came fleeing alone on horseback; the Emperor pardoned and enrolled him, making him campaigning staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhengzhou fell to the Cai rebels; Prefect Li Fan fled alone on horseback; he pardoned him and made him campaigning staff officer.

sentences.zh: 宗權既得鄭，益驕，帝遣裨將邏于金隄驛，與賊相遇，因擊之，賊眾大敗，追至武陽橋，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Once Zongquan had taken Zheng he grew more arrogant; the Emperor sent a subordinate general to patrol at Jindi Post, met the bandits, and struck them; the rebel horde suffered a great defeat; they pursued them to Wuyang Bridge and cut off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by taking Zheng, Zongquan grew arrogant; a patrol at Jindi Post routed his men and pursued them to Wuyang Bridge, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 帝每與蔡人戰於四郊，既以少擊眾，常出奇以制之，但患師少，未快其旨。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor fought the men of Cai on the four outskirts, because he used the few to strike the many he often employed surprise to control them, but he only worried that his forces were too few and could not fully satisfy his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting the Cai men in the suburbs with inferior numbers, he relied on surprise, but always wished for more troops.

sentences.zh: 宗權又以己眾十倍於帝，恥於頻敗，乃誓眾堅決以攻夷門。

translations.literal: Zongquan also, because his forces were ten times the Emperor's, was shamed by frequent defeat and therefore swore his masses to a firm resolve to attack Yimen.
translations.idiomatic: Shamed by repeated defeat despite outnumbering him ten to one, Zongquan swore his army to a final assault on Yimen.

sentences.zh: 既而獲蔡之諜者，備知其事，遂謀濟師焉。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they captured a spy of Cai and learned the whole affair in detail, and thereupon planned to bring in reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing a Cai spy, he learned the plan and set about raising reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 三年春二月乙巳，承制以朱珍為淄州刺史，俾募兵於東道，且慮蔡人暴其麥苗，期以夏首回歸。

translations.literal: On yisi day of the second month of the spring of the third year, by imperial commission Zhu Zhen was made prefect of Zi Prefecture, so that he might recruit troops on the eastern circuit, and because they feared the Cai men would ravage the wheat seedlings, they set the time of return for the beginning of summer.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the second month of the third year he commissioned Zhu Zhen prefect of Zi to recruit on the eastern circuit, planning to return by early summer before the Cai men could trample the wheat.

sentences.zh: 珍既至淄、棣，旬日之內，應募者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Once Zhen had reached Zi and Di, within ten days more than ten thousand men answered the call.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days at Zi and Di he raised more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 又潛襲青州，獲馬千匹，鎧甲稱是，乃鼓行而歸。

translations.literal: He also secretly raided Qing Prefecture, obtained a thousand horses, and armor in proportion; he then marched back with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: He also raided Qingzhou for a thousand horses and matching armor, then marched back in triumph.

sentences.zh: 四月辛亥，達於夷門。

translations.literal: On xinhai day of the fourth month he reached Yimen.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day in the fourth month he reached Yimen.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「吾事濟矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor rejoiced and said, "My affair is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "My cause is saved.

sentences.zh: 」是時，賊將張晊屯於北郊，秦賢屯於版橋，各有眾數萬，樹柵相連二十餘里，其勢甚盛。

translations.literal: " At that time the rebel general Zhang Zhi was encamped at the northern suburb and Qin Xian at Banqiao, each with tens of thousands of men; they built stockades linked for more than twenty li, and their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Zhi held the northern suburbs and Qin Xian Banqiao, each with tens of thousands in camps strung twenty li, and their strength seemed overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「此賊方今息師蓄銳以俟時，必來攻我。

translations.literal: The Emperor told the generals, "These bandits are now resting their troops and storing their edge to await the moment; they are sure to come attack us.
translations.idiomatic: He told his generals, "The enemy is resting and sharpening his edge; he will surely attack us.

sentences.zh: 況宗權度我兵少，又未知珍來，謂吾畏懼，止於堅守而已。

translations.literal: Moreover Zongquan gauged our few troops and also did not yet know that Zhen had come; he thought we were afraid and would only hold firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan thinks us few, does not know Zhen has arrived, and expects us only to cower behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 今出不意，不如先擊之。

translations.literal: Now, striking where they do not expect it, it would be better to attack them first.
translations.idiomatic: Strike before he expects it—attack first.

sentences.zh: 」乃親引兵攻秦賢寨，將士踴躍爭先，賊果不備，連拔四寨，斬首萬餘級，時賊眾以為神助。

translations.literal: " He then personally led troops to attack Qin Xian's stockade; officers and soldiers leaped forward competing to be first; the bandits were indeed unprepared; they successively took four stockades and cut off more than ten thousand heads; at that time the rebel masses regarded it as divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the assault on Qin Xian's camp himself; his men rushed the unprepared rebels, took four camps in succession, and killed more than ten thousand—the enemy thought heaven fought for him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賊將盧瑭領萬餘人于圃田北萬勝戍，夾汴水為營，跨河為梁，以扼運路。

translations.literal: On gengwu day the rebel general Lu Yan led more than ten thousand men at Wansheng garrison north of Putian, made camps on both banks of the Bian River, and spanned the river with a bridge to choke the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Lu Yan held Wansheng garrison north of Putian with ten thousand men, camped on both banks of the Bian River, and bridged it to choke supply lines.

sentences.zh: 帝擇精銳以襲之。

translations.literal: The Emperor chose crack troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He chose elite troops for a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 是日昏霧四合，兵及賊壘方覺，遂突入掩殺，赴水死者甚眾，盧瑭自投於河。

translations.literal: That day the four quarters were wrapped in dusk fog; the soldiers reached the rebel stockade before they were noticed; they then burst in to cover and kill; very many died in the water; Lu Yan himself threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk fog hid the assault until they were on the camp; they slaughtered the garrison; many drowned; Lu Yan threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 河南諸賊連敗，不敢復駐，皆並在張晊寨。

translations.literal: The bandits of Henan, defeated in succession, did not dare stay again; all gathered in Zhang Zhi's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated rebels across Henan fled to Zhang Zhi's camp.

sentences.zh: 自是蔡寇皆懷震讋，往往軍中自相驚亂。

translations.literal: From then on the men of Cai all harbored dread and trembling, and often in the army they alarmed one another.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Cai army shook with fear and panicked at shadows.

sentences.zh: 帝旋師休息，大行犒賞，由是軍士各懷憤激，每遇敵，無不奮勇。

translations.literal: The Emperor withdrew his army to rest and carried out great rewards and feasts; thereby the soldiers each harbored fierce zeal, and whenever they met the enemy there was none who did not fight bravely.
translations.idiomatic: He rested his army and lavished rewards until every soldier burned to fight.

sentences.zh: 五月丙子，出酸棗門，自卯至未，短兵相接，賊眾大敗，追斬二十餘里，僵僕就枕。

translations.literal: On bingzi day of the fifth month he went out through the Suanzao Gate; from mao to wei they fought hand to hand at close quarters; the rebel masses suffered a great defeat; they pursued and cut them down for more than twenty li; the fallen lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the fifth month he sallied from Suanzao Gate and from mao to wei fought hand to hand; the rebels broke; pursuit ran twenty li with the dead piled like pillows.

sentences.zh: 宗權恥敗，益縱其虐，乃自鄭州親領突將數人，徑入張晊寨。

translations.literal: Zongquan, shamed by defeat, grew more wanton in his cruelty; he himself from Zheng Prefecture led a few picked shock troops and went straight into Zhang Zhi's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Zongquan turned more savage and rode from Zhengzhou with picked raiders into Zhang Zhi's camp.

sentences.zh: 其日晚，大星隕於賊壘，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: That evening a great star fell in the rebel stockade with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: That evening a great star fell on the rebel camp with a thunderous crash.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，兗、鄆、滑軍士皆來赴援，乃陳兵于汴水之上，旌旗器甲甚盛。

translations.literal: On xinsi day the soldiers of Yan, Yun, and Hua all came to bring relief; they then arrayed troops on the Bian River; banners, flags, weapons, and armor were very splendid.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day reinforcements from Yan, Yun, and Hua arrived; he paraded them on the Bian River in splendid array.

sentences.zh: 蔡人望之，不敢出寨。

translations.literal: The men of Cai gazed at them and did not dare leave the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai men looked on and dared not leave their camp.

sentences.zh: 翌日，分佈諸軍，齊攻賊寨，自寅至申，斬首二萬餘級。

translations.literal: The next day he deployed the armies and attacked the rebel stockades together; from the yin hour to the shen hour they cut off more than twenty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he arrayed his forces for a joint assault on the rebel camps; from yin to shen they took more than twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 會夜收軍，獲牛馬、輜重、生口、器甲不可勝計。

translations.literal: At nightfall he withdrew the army, having seized cattle, horses, baggage trains, captives, and armor beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: At night he drew off the army with cattle, horses, supplies, prisoners, and arms in incalculable quantity.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宗權、晊遁去，遲明追之，至陽武橋而還。

translations.literal: That night Zongquan and Zhi fled; at first light he pursued them to Yangwu Bridge and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zongquan and Zhi escaped; at dawn he pursued them to Yangwu Bridge and turned back.

sentences.zh: 宗權至鄭州，乃盡焚其廬舍，屠其郡人而去。

translations.literal: When Zongquan reached Zheng Prefecture he burned every dwelling, slaughtered the people of the prefecture, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Zhengzhou, Zongquan burned the city to the ground, massacred its people, and fled.

sentences.zh: 始蔡人分兵寇陝、洛、孟、懷、許、汝，皆先據之，因是敗也，賊眾恐懼，鹹棄之而遁。

translations.literal: At first the men of Cai had divided their forces to raid Shan, Luo, Meng, Huai, Xu, and Ru, and had all seized them first; because of this defeat the rebel masses were terrified and all abandoned them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai rebels had earlier garrisoned Shan, Luoyang, Meng, Huai, Xu, and Ru; now, shattered in defeat, they abandoned every post and fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 帝乃慎選將佐，俾完葺壁壘，為戰守之備，於是遠近流亡復歸者眾矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor then carefully chose generals and aides and had them repair the walls and ramparts and prepare for war and defense; thereupon many refugees near and far returned.
translations.idiomatic: He chose his officers with care, had the walls restored and defenses readied, and refugees streamed back from far and near.

sentences.zh: 是時，揚州節度使高駢為裨將畢師鐸所害，復有孫儒、楊行密互相攻伐，朝廷不能制，乃就加帝檢校太尉，兼領淮南節度使。

translations.literal: At that time the military governor of Yangzhou, Gao Pian, had been killed by his vice-general Bi Shiduo; Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi were again attacking one another, and the court could not control them; the court thereupon added to the Emperor the acting post of Grand Commandant and concurrently made him military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian of Yangzhou had fallen to Bi Shiduo; Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi were tearing Huainan apart beyond the court's control, and the throne therefore promoted the emperor to acting Grand Commandant with concurrent command of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 九月，亳州裨將謝殷逐刺史宋袞，自據其郡；

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Bozhou vice-general Xie Yin expelled the prefect Song Gun and seized the prefecture for himself;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Xie Yin, a Bozhou officer, drove out Prefect Song Gun and seized the commandery;

sentences.zh: 帝親領軍屯于太清宮，遣霍存討平之。

translations.literal: the Emperor personally led his army to encamp at the Supreme Unity Palace and sent Huo Cun to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor marched in person to the Supreme Unity Palace and sent Huo Cun to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 帝之禦蔡寇也，鄆州朱瑄、兗州朱瑾皆領兵來援。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was resisting the Cai bandits, Zhu Xuan of Yan Prefecture and Zhu Jin of Yun Prefecture had both led troops to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: While he fought the Cai rebels, Zhu Xuan of Yanzhou and Zhu Jin of Yunzhou both marched to his aid.

sentences.zh: 及宗權既敗，帝以瑄、瑾宗人也，又有力於己，皆厚禮以歸之。

translations.literal: After Zongquan was defeated, the Emperor, considering that Xuan and Jin were men of his clan and had exerted themselves on his behalf, treated them with generous rites and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongquan's defeat he sent Xuan and Jin home with rich honors—they were kinsmen who had fought for him.

sentences.zh: 瑄、瑾以帝軍士勇悍，私心愛之，乃密于曹、濮界上懸金帛以誘之，帝軍利其貨而赴者甚眾，帝乃移檄以讓之。

translations.literal: Xuan and Jin, because the Emperor's soldiers were fierce and bold, privately admired them; they secretly hung gold and silks on the Cao–Pu border to lure them, and very many of the Emperor's troops went for the goods; the Emperor then sent a written protest rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring his fierce troops, Xuan and Jin secretly offered gold and silk on the Cao–Pu border to lure deserters; so many men went that the emperor rebuked them in writing.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄來詞不遜，乃命朱珍侵曹伐濮，以懲其奸。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan came with insolent words; the Emperor then ordered Zhu Zhen to invade Cao and attack Pu to punish their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan answered with insolence; the emperor sent Zhu Zhen into Cao and Pu to punish their treachery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，珍伐曹州，執刺史丘禮以獻，遂移兵圍濮。

translations.literal: Before long Zhen attacked Cao Prefecture, seized the prefect Qiu Li and presented him, then shifted his troops to besiege Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Zhen took Cao, captured Prefect Qiu Li, and turned to besiege Pu.

sentences.zh: 兗、鄆之釁，自茲而始矣。

translations.literal: The strife of Yan and Yun began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The feud between Yan and Yun began here.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒考異》引高若拙《後史補》云：「梁太祖皇帝到梁園，深有大志。

translations.literal: The 《Examination of Discrepancies in the Comprehensive Mirror》 cites Gao Ruozhuo's 《Supplement to the Later History》, saying: "When the Founding Emperor of Liang arrived at Liang Garden, his ambition ran very deep.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Zizhi Tongjian: Examination of Discrepancies》 quotes Gao Ruozhuo's 《Supplement to the Later History》: "When Liang's founding emperor came to Liang Garden, his ambition burned bright.

sentences.zh: 然兵力不足，常欲外掠；

translations.literal: Yet his troops were insufficient and he often wished to raid outward;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his forces were too few, and he longed to raid beyond his borders;

sentences.zh: 又虞四境之難，每有鬱然之狀。

translations.literal: he also feared trouble on the four frontiers and often wore a troubled look.
translations.idiomatic: yet he feared attack from every side and often looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 時有薦敬秀才于門下，乃白梁祖曰：'明公方欲圖大事，輜重必為四境所侵。

translations.literal: At that time someone recommended the scholar Jing at his gate; he reported to the Liang Ancestor, saying: "My lord now wishes to accomplish a great affair; your baggage train will surely be harried on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then recommended Scholar Jing, who told the Liang founder: "My lord aims at great things, yet your baggage will be prey on every frontier.

sentences.zh: 但令麾下將士詐為叛者而逃，即明公奏於主上，及告四鄰，以自襲叛徒為名。

translations.literal: Only order your generals to feign desertion and flee; then my lord can memorialize the sovereign and inform the four neighbors, taking as your pretext that you yourself are attacking deserters.
translations.idiomatic: Let your officers pretend to desert and flee; then report to the throne and the neighboring powers that you are punishing traitors in your own ranks.

sentences.zh: '梁祖曰：'天降奇人，以佐於吾。

translations.literal: " The Liang Ancestor said: "Heaven has sent me an extraordinary man to assist me.
translations.idiomatic: " The founder replied: "Heaven has sent me a wonder to aid my cause.

sentences.zh: '初從其議，一出而致眾十倍。」

translations.literal: " At first he followed this plan; with one sortie his forces increased tenfold."
translations.idiomatic: " He took the counsel; one raid swelled his army tenfold."

sentences.zh: 十月，僖宗命水部郎中王贊撰紀功碑以賜帝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Emperor Xizong ordered the Director of the Waterways Bureau Wang Zan to compose a stele recording merit and bestow it on the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xizong ordered Wang Zan of the Waterways Bureau to compose a merit stele and bestow it on the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝親帥騎數千巡師於濮上，因破朱瑄援師于範縣。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor personally led several thousand horsemen to review the army on the Pu frontier and thereby defeated Zhu Xuan's relief force at Fan County.
translations.idiomatic: That month he led several thousand horsemen on patrol along the Pu front and routed Zhu Xuan's relief column at Fan County.

sentences.zh: 丁未，攻陷濮州，刺史朱裕單騎奔鄆。

translations.literal: On dingwei day he stormed Pu Prefecture; the prefect Zhu Yu fled alone on horseback to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he took Pu; Prefect Zhu Yu rode alone to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為鄆人所敗，逾月乃還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was defeated by the men of Yun; only after more than a month did he return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the men of Yun defeated him, and he did not return for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 十二月，僖宗遣使賜帝鐵券，又命翰林承旨劉崇望撰德政碑以賜帝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Emperor Xizong sent envoys to bestow on the Emperor an iron writ of immunity; he also ordered the Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance Liu Chongwang to compose a stele of virtuous governance and bestow it on the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xizong sent an iron certificate of grace and had Liu Chongwang, Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, compose a stele praising his governance.

sentences.zh: 閏月甲寅。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, jiayin day.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, jiayin day.

sentences.zh: 帝請行營司馬李璠權知淮南留後，乃遣大將郭言領兵援送以赴揚州。

translations.literal: The Emperor requested that the campaign staff officer Li Fan be made acting regent of Huainan; he then sent the great general Guo Yan to lead troops in escort to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Li Fan serve as acting regent of Huainan and sent Guo Yan with an escort to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，昭宗制以帝檢校侍中，增食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: On jihai day of the fifth month Emperor Zhaozong appointed the Emperor acting Palace Attendant and increased his fief by three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the fifth month Zhaozong made him acting Palace Attendant and added three thousand households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，昭改帝鄉衣錦，裏曰沛王裏。

translations.literal: On wuchen day Zhao changed the Emperor's home district Returning in Splendor and its village to Prince of Pei Village.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he renamed the emperor's home district "Returning in Splendor" and its hamlet Prince of Pei Hamlet.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝以兼有洛、孟之地，無西顧之患，將大整師徒，畢力誅蔡。

translations.literal: That month, because the Emperor now held the lands of Luo and Meng and had no worry on the western front, he was about to reorganize his army in full strength to exterminate Cai.
translations.idiomatic: That month, secure in Luo and Meng and free of western threats, he prepared to marshal his full strength against Cai.

sentences.zh: 會蔡人趙德諲舉漢南之地以歸於朝廷，且遣使送款於帝，仍誓戮力同討宗權。

translations.literal: It happened that the Cai leader Zhao Deyin offered the lands of southern Han to the court and moreover sent envoys to pledge loyalty to the Emperor, still vowing to join forces in attacking Zongquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deyin of Cai then surrendered southern Han to the court, sent envoys to the emperor, and pledged to join him against Zongquan.

sentences.zh: 帝表其事，朝廷因以德諲為蔡州四面副都統。

translations.literal: The Emperor memorialized the matter; the court thereupon made Deyin Deputy Commander-in-Chief on the four sides of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reported this, and the court made Deyin deputy commander on all four sides of Cai.

sentences.zh: 又以河陽、保義、義昌三節度為帝行軍司馬，兼糧料應接。

translations.literal: The three military governorships of Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang were also made the Emperor's campaign staff officers, jointly supplying grain and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang were also assigned as his campaign staff, charged with grain and supply.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝領諸侯之師會德諲以伐蔡賊于汝水之上，遂薄其城。

translations.literal: By this time the Emperor led the armies of the feudal lords to join Deyin in attacking the Cai bandits on the Ru River and pressed close to the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the allied hosts with Deyin to the Ru River, where they pressed the Cai rebels against their walls.

sentences.zh: 五日之內，樹二十八寨以環之，蓋象列宿之數也。

translations.literal: Within five days he raised twenty-eight stockades to encircle it, emulating the number of the lunar mansions.
translations.idiomatic: In five days he ringed the city with twenty-eight camps—the number of the lunar mansions.

sentences.zh: 時帝親臨矢石，一日，飛矢中其左腋，血漬單衣，顧謂左右曰：「勿泄。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor personally came under flying arrows; one day a stray arrow struck his left armpit and blood soaked his single robe; he turned to those beside him and said, "Do not reveal this.
translations.idiomatic: He stood in the arrow storm himself; one day a shaft struck his left armpit and blood soaked his tunic. He told his attendants, "Tell no one.

sentences.zh: 」九月，以糧運不繼，遂班師。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month, because grain transport could not be sustained, he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month, with supplies failing, he drew off the army.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝知宗權殘孽不足為患，遂移兵以伐徐。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor knew that Zongquan's remnant followers were no great trouble; he then shifted his troops to attack Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Zongquan's remnants no longer dangerous, he turned his army against Xu.

sentences.zh: 十月，先遣朱珍領兵與時溥戰于吳康鎮，徐人大敗，連收豐、蕭二邑；

translations.literal: In the tenth month he first sent Zhu Zhen to lead troops to fight Shi Pu at Wukang Post; the men of Xu suffered a great defeat, and he successively recovered the districts of Feng and Xiao;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent Zhu Zhen against Shi Pu at Wukang; the Xu army broke, and Feng and Xiao fell in succession;

sentences.zh: 溥攜散騎馳入彭門。

translations.literal: Pu, clutching his seal of office, galloped into Peng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Pu fled on horseback into Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 帝命分兵以攻宿州，刺史張友攜符印以降。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered his forces divided to attack Suzhou; the prefect Zhang You came bearing his seal and ribbon to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns against Suzhou; Prefect Zhang You came out with seal and ribbon to surrender.

sentences.zh: 既而徐人閉壁堅守，遂命龐師古屯兵守之而還。

translations.literal: Before long the men of Xu closed their walls and held firm; he then ordered Pang Shigu to garrison troops and hold them while he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu men then shut themselves behind the walls; he left Pang Shigu to hold the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是月，蔡賊孫儒攻陷揚州，自稱淮南節度使。

translations.literal: That month the Cai bandit Sun Ru stormed Yangzhou and styled himself military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: That month Sun Ru of Cai took Yangzhou and proclaimed himself military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 大順元年四月丙辰，宿州小將張筠逐刺史張紹光，擁眾以附時溥。

translations.literal: On bingchen day of the fourth month of the first year of Dashun, the Suzhou minor officer Zhang Yun expelled the prefect Zhang Shaoguang and led the masses to join Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In Dashun 1.4, on bingchen, Zhang Yun, a junior officer at Suzhou, drove out Prefect Zhang Shaoguang and went over to Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 帝率親軍討之，殺千餘人，筠遂堅守。

translations.literal: The Emperor led his personal army to attack him, killed more than a thousand men, and Yun then held firm behind his walls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched in person, killed more than a thousand men, and Yun held the walls.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，時溥出兵暴碭山縣，帝遣朱友裕以兵襲之，敗徐軍三千餘眾，獲沙陀援軍石君和等三十人，斬於宿州城下。

translations.literal: On yimao day Shi Pu sent troops to raid Dangshan County; the Emperor sent Zhu Youyu with troops to strike them, defeated more than three thousand men of the Xu army, captured the Shatuo relief officer Shi Junhe and thirty others, and beheaded them below the wall of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Shi Pu raided Dangshan; the emperor sent Zhu Youyu, broke three thousand Xu troops, and beheaded thirty captives—including the Shatuo officer Shi Junhe—below the walls of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月辛酉，淮南孫儒遣使修好於帝，帝表其事，請以淮南節度授於儒焉。

translations.literal: On xinyou day of the sixth month Sun Ru of Huainan sent envoys to seek good relations with the Emperor; the Emperor memorialized the matter and requested that the Huainan governorship be granted to Ru.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the sixth month Sun Ru sent envoys seeking peace; the emperor memorialized that Huainan be granted to him.

sentences.zh: 辛未，昭宗命帝為宣義軍節度使，充河東東面行營招討使，時朝廷宰臣張浚將兵討太原故也。

translations.literal: On xinwei day Emperor Zhaozong appointed the Emperor military governor of the Xuanyi Army and commander of the eastern Hedong campaign, because the court's chief minister Zhang Jun was then leading troops to attack Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Zhaozong made him military governor of Xuanyi and commander of the eastern campaign against Hedong, for Chief Minister Zhang Jun was marching on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 八月甲寅，昭義都將馮霸殺沙陀所署節度使李克恭來降，帝請河陽節度使硃崇節為潞州留後。

translations.literal: On jiayin day of the eighth month Feng Ba, a general of Zhaoyi, killed the military governor appointed by the Shatuo, Li Ke Gong, and came to surrender; the Emperor requested that Zhu Chongjie of Heyang be made regent of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the eighth month Feng Ba of Zhaoyi killed Li Ke Gong, the Shatuo appointee, and surrendered; the emperor asked that Zhu Chongjie of Heyang hold Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，李克用自率蕃漢步騎數萬以圍潞州，帝遣葛從周率驍勇之士，夜中銜枚犯圍而入於潞。

translations.literal: On wuchen day Li Keyong himself led tens of thousands of steppe and Han infantry and cavalry to besiege Lu Prefecture; the Emperor sent Ge Congzhou with fierce warriors to enter Lu at midnight with gags in their mouths, breaking through the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Li Keyong himself invested Luzhou with tens of thousands of steppe and Chinese horse and foot; the emperor sent Ge Congzhou with picked men to slip through the siege at midnight, gags in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，帝至河陽，遣部將李讜引軍趨澤、潞，行至馬牢川，為晉人所敗。

translations.literal: On renyin day of the ninth month the Emperor reached Heyang and sent his subordinate general Li Dan to hurry toward Ze and Lu; when they reached Malao River they were defeated by the Jin men.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the ninth month he reached Heyang and sent Li Dan toward Ze and Lu; at Malao River the Jin army broke him.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣朱友裕、張全義率精兵至鄆州北以為應援。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Zhu Youyu and Zhang Quanyi with elite troops to the north of Yun Prefecture as relief.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhu Youyu and Zhang Quanyi with elite troops north of Yunzhou as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 既而崇節、從周棄潞來歸。

translations.literal: Before long Chongjie and Congzhou abandoned Lu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chongjie and Congzhou abandoned Luzhou and came home.

sentences.zh: 戊申，帝廷責諸將敗軍之罪，斬李讜、李重允以徇，遂班師焉。

translations.literal: On wushen day the Emperor rebuked the generals in open court for the defeat of the army, executed Li Dan and Li Chongyun as examples, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he rebuked his generals in open court for the defeat, executed Li Dan and Li Chongyun as examples, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十月乙酉，帝自河陽赴滑台。

translations.literal: On yiyou day of the tenth month the Emperor went from Heyang to Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the tenth month he went from Heyang to Huatai.

sentences.zh: 時奉詔將討太原，先遣使假道于魏，魏人不從。

translations.literal: At that time, having received the edict to campaign against Taiyuan, he first sent envoys to request passage through Wei; the men of Wei would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Under orders to attack Taiyuan, he first asked passage through Wei; Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝遣行人雷鄴告糴于魏，既而為牙軍所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had sent the envoy Lei Ye to announce a grain purchase in Wei; afterward he was killed by the yajun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had sent Lei Ye to Wei to buy grain; the guard soldiery killed him.

sentences.zh: 羅宏信懼，故不敢從命，遂通好於太原。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin was afraid and therefore dared not obey the command; he then opened good relations with Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin, in fear, defied the order and made peace with Taiyuan instead.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛丑，帝遣丁會、葛從周率眾渡河取黎陽、臨河，又令龐師古、霍存下淇門、衛縣，帝徐以大軍繼其後。

translations.literal: On xinchou day of the twelfth month the Emperor sent Ding Hui and Ge Congzhou to lead the masses across the river and take Liyang and Linhe; he also ordered Pang Shigu and Huo Cun to descend on Qimen and Wei County, while the Emperor himself slowly followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the twelfth month Ding Hui and Ge Congzhou crossed the river and took Liyang and Linhe; Pang Shigu and Huo Cun took Qimen and Weixian; the emperor followed with the main host.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，魏軍屯于內黃。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the Wei army encamped at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, the Wei army camped at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝與之接戰，自內黃至永定橋，魏軍五敗，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: On bingchen day the Emperor joined battle with them from Neihuang to Yongding Bridge; the Wei army was defeated five times and more than ten thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he fought them from Neihuang to Yongding Bridge; the Wei army lost five battles and more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 羅宏信懼，遣使持厚幣請和。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin was afraid and sent envoys bearing rich gifts to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin, terrified, sent envoys with rich gifts to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 帝命止其焚掠而歸其俘，宏信由是感悅而聽命焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that burning and plunder cease and captives be returned; Hongxin was thereby moved to gratitude and submitted to his commands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted the burning, returned prisoners, and Hongxin submitted in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 乃收軍屯於河上。

translations.literal: He then withdrew the army and encamped on the river bank.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew and camped on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 八月己丑，帝遣丁會急攻宿州，刺史張筠堅守其壁，會乃率眾於州東築堰，壅汴水以浸其城。

translations.literal: On jichou day of the eighth month the Emperor sent Ding Hui to press the attack on Suzhou; the prefect Zhang Yun held firm behind his walls; Hui then led the masses to build a dam east of the prefecture and dammed the Bian River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the eighth month Ding Hui pressed Suzhou; Prefect Zhang Yun held the walls while Hui's men built a dam east of the city and diverted the Bian River to flood it.

sentences.zh: 十月壬午，筠遂降，宿州平。

translations.literal: On renyang day of the tenth month Yun then surrendered and Suzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On renyang in the tenth month Yun surrendered and Suzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁未，曹州裨將郭紹賓殺刺史郭饒，舉郡來降。

translations.literal: On dingwei day of the eleventh month the Cao vice-general Guo Shaobin killed the prefect Guo Rao and led the whole prefecture to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the eleventh month Guo Shaobin, a Cao officer, killed Prefect Guo Rao and surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 是月，徐將劉知俊率眾二千來降，自是徐軍不振。

translations.literal: That month the Xu general Liu Zhijun led two thousand men to surrender; from this the Xu army no longer flourished.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Zhijun of Xu came over with two thousand men, and Xu's strength never recovered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，兗州朱瑾領軍三萬寇單父，帝遣丁會領大軍襲敗之敗于金鄉界，殺二萬餘眾，瑾單馬遁去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zhu Jin of Yan led thirty thousand men to raid Shanfu; the Emperor sent Ding Hui with the main army to strike and defeat them at the border of Jinxiang; more than twenty thousand were killed and Jin fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhu Jin of Yan raided Shanfu with thirty thousand men; Ding Hui met him at Jinxiang, killed more than twenty thousand, and Jin fled alone.

sentences.zh: 二年四月丁丑，龐師古下彭門，梟時溥首以獻。

translations.literal: On dingchou day of the fourth month of the second year Pang Shigu took Peng Gate and displayed Shi Pu's head as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on dingchou in the fourth month, Pang Shigu took Pengcheng and sent up Shi Pu's head.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝遣龐師古移兵攻兗，駐於曲阜，與朱瑾屢戰，皆敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Emperor sent Pang Shigu to shift troops and attack Yan, encamping at Qufu; he fought Zhu Jin repeatedly and defeated him each time.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Pang Shigu against Yan; camped at Qufu, Pang defeated Zhu Jin again and again.

sentences.zh: 十二月，師古遣先鋒葛從周引軍以攻齊州，刺史朱威告急於兗、鄆。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Shigu sent the vanguard Ge Congzhou to lead troops and attack Qi Prefecture; the prefect Zhu Wei sent urgent word to Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Pang sent Ge Congzhou against Qizhou; Prefect Zhu Wei cried for aid to Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 既而朱瑄以援兵至，遂固其壘。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu Xuan came with relief troops and then fortified his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan came with relief and fortified his camp.

sentences.zh: 乾甯元年二月，帝親領大軍由鄆州東路北次於魚山。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianning the Emperor personally led the main army east along the road from Yun Prefecture and halted at Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 1.2 the emperor led his main force east from Yanzhou and halted at Yushan.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄覘知，即以兵徑至，且圖速戰。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan detected it and came straight on, moreover seeking a swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan learned of it, marched straight at him, and sought a quick fight.

sentences.zh: 帝整軍出寨，時瑄、瑾已陣於前，須臾，東南風大起，我軍旌旗失次，甚有懼色，即令騎士揚鞭呼嘯。

translations.literal: The Emperor arrayed his army and went out of the stockade; at that time Xuan and Jin had already formed their battle lines in front; in a moment a great southeast wind arose, our army's banners and flags lost their order, and there was much fear; he thereupon ordered the horsemen to raise their whips and shout.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up outside the camp while Xuan and Jin were already formed before him. A fierce southeast wind threw his banners into confusion and fear spread; he ordered his horsemen to crack their whips and shout.

sentences.zh: 俄而西北風驟發，時兩軍皆在草莽中，帝因令縱火。

translations.literal: Before long a northwest wind suddenly sprang up; at that time both armies were in the grass and scrub; the Emperor thereupon ordered fire set.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a northwest gale rose. Both armies stood in dry grass; the emperor ordered the field set ablaze.

sentences.zh: 既而煙焰亙天，乘勢以攻賊陣，瑄、瑾大敗。

translations.literal: Before long smoke and flames filled the sky; seizing the momentum he attacked the rebel battle lines, and Xuan and Jin suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Smoke blotted out the sky; he drove into the enemy line and broke Xuan and Jin completely.

sentences.zh: 殺萬餘人，餘眾擁入清河，因築京觀於魚山之下，駐軍數日而還。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand were killed; the remainder were driven into the Qing River; he then built a victory mound below Yushan, encamped several days, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He killed more than ten thousand; the rest were driven into the Qing River. He raised a victory mound below Yushan, camped several days, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二年正月癸亥，遣朱友恭帥師復伐兗，遂塹而圍之。

translations.literal: On guihai day of the first month of the second year he sent Zhu Yougong to lead troops again to attack Yan and thereupon invested it with trenches.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the second year, first month, he sent Zhu Yougong to besiege Yan with trenches.

sentences.zh: 未幾，朱瑄自鄆率步騎援糧欲入于兗，友恭設伏以敗之，盡奪其餉于高吳，因擒蕃將安福順、安福慶。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu Xuan led infantry and cavalry from Yun with relief grain intending to enter Yan; Yougong set an ambush and defeated them, seizing all their provisions at Gaowu, and thereby captured the barbarian generals An Fushun and An Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Xuan marched from Yanzhou with grain for the relief of Yan; Yougong ambushed him at Gaowu, seized the supplies, and captured the barbarian generals An Fushun and An Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 二月己酉，帝領親軍屯于單父，以為友恭之援。

translations.literal: On jiyou day of the second month the Emperor led his personal army to encamp at Shanfu as relief for Yougong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the second month he camped at Shanfu to support Yougong.

sentences.zh: 四月，濠、壽二州復為楊行密所陷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Hao and Shou were again lost to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yang Xingmi retook Hao and Shou.

sentences.zh: 是時，太原遣將史儼兒、李承嗣以萬騎馳入於鄆。

translations.literal: At that time Taiyuan sent the generals Shi Yan'er and Li Chengsi with ten thousand horsemen galloping into Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan then sent Shi Yan'er and Li Chengsi with ten thousand horsemen into Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱友恭遂歸於汴。

translations.literal: Zhu Yougong thereupon returned to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong withdrew to Bian.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝領親軍伐鄆，至大仇，遣前軍挑戰，設伏於梁山以待之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Emperor led his personal army to attack Yun, reaching Daqiu; he sent the vanguard to offer challenge and set an ambush at Liangshan to await them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he marched on Yanzhou as far as Daqiu, sent his vanguard to provoke battle, and laid an ambush at Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 既而獲蕃將史完府，奪馬數百匹。

translations.literal: Before long they captured the barbarian general Shi Wanfu and seized several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the barbarian officer Shi Wanfu and took several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄脫身遁去，復入於鄆。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan slipped away and fled, again entering Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan escaped and fled back into Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝駐軍于鄆，齊州刺史朱瓊遣使請降，瓊即瑾之從父兄也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor encamped at Yun; the Qi Prefecture prefect Zhu Qiong sent envoys to request surrender—Qiong was Jin's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he camped at Yanzhou; Zhu Qiong of Qizhou offered surrender—he was Zhu Jin's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 帝因移軍至兗，瓊果來降。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon shifted his army to Yan; Qiong indeed came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Yan, and Qiong came in as promised.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瓊為朱瑾所紿，掠而殺之，帝即以其弟玭為齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long Qiong was deceived by Zhu Jin, seized and killed; the Emperor thereupon made his younger brother Min defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin tricked Qiong, seized him, and killed him; the emperor appointed his younger brother Min defender of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，朱瑄復遣將賀瑰、柳存及蕃將何懷寶等萬餘人以襲曹州，庶解兗州之圍也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhu Xuan again sent the generals He Gui, Liu Cun, and the barbarian general He Huaibao and more than ten thousand men to raid Cao Prefecture, hoping thereby to relieve the siege of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhu Xuan sent He Gui, Liu Cun, and the barbarian He Huaibao with more than ten thousand men to raid Cao and break the siege of Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，自兗領軍策馬先路至钜野南，追而敗之，殺戮將盡，生擒賀瑰、柳存、何懷寶及賊党三千餘人。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it; he himself led the army from Yan, spurring his horse ahead to the south of Juye, pursued and defeated them, slaughtered nearly all, and captured alive He Gui, Liu Cun, He Huaibao, and more than three thousand of the rebel party.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, he rode ahead from Yan to south of Juye, overtook them, slaughtered nearly all, and took He Gui, Liu Cun, He Huaibao, and more than three thousand alive.

sentences.zh: 是日申時，狂風暴起，沙塵沸湧，帝曰：「此乃殺人未足耳。

translations.literal: At the shen hour of that day a fierce wind suddenly arose and sand and dust boiled up; the Emperor said, "This means the killing is not yet enough.
translations.idiomatic: At the shen hour that day a wild wind rose and sand boiled up. The emperor said, "This means we have not killed enough.

sentences.zh: 」遂下令盡殺所獲囚俘，風亦止焉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered that all the prisoners taken be put to death, and the wind then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered every captive killed, and the wind fell still.

sentences.zh: 翼日，縶賀瑰等以示於兗。

translations.literal: The next day he bound He Gui and the others and displayed them at Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he bound He Gui and the others and paraded them before Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝素知瑰名，乃釋之，惟斬何懷寶於兗城之下，乃班師。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long known Gui's name; he then released him, beheading only He Huaibao below the wall of Yan, and thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Gui's name, he spared him, beheaded only He Huaibao below the walls of Yan, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二月，葛從周領兵復伐兗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Ge Congzhou led troops again to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Ge Congzhou marched again against Yan.

sentences.zh: 既至，與朱瑾戰於壘下，殺千餘眾，擒其將孫漢筠已下二十人，遂旋師。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he fought Zhu Jin below the stockade, killed more than a thousand men, captured the general Sun Hanjun and twenty men below him, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he fought Zhu Jin at the ramparts, killed more than a thousand, captured Sun Hanjun and twenty officers, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，河東李克用既破邠州，欲謀爭霸，乃遣蕃將張汙落以萬騎寨于河北之莘縣，聲言欲救兗、鄆。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Li Keyong of Hedong, having already taken Bin Prefecture and wishing to contend for supremacy, sent the barbarian general Zhang Wuluo with ten thousand cavalry to encamp at Shen County in Hebei, proclaiming that he meant to rescue Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Keyong of Hedong, having seized Binzhou and bent on hegemony, sent the barbarian Zhang Wuluo with ten thousand horse to camp at Shen County in Hebei, claiming he would relieve Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使羅宏信患之，使來求援。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin, military governor of Weibo, was troubled by this and sent to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo's governor Luo Hongxin, alarmed, begged for help.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝領親軍屯于單父，會寒食，帝乃親拜文穆皇帝陵于碭日縣午溝裏。

translations.literal: In the second month the Emperor led his personal army to camp at Shanfu; it coincided with Cold Food Festival, and the Emperor personally paid respects at the tomb of Emperor Wenmu at Wugou village in Dangri County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he camped his personal army at Shanfu; during Cold Food Festival he visited his father Wenmu's tomb at Wugou in Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 四月辛酉，河東泛漲，將壞滑城。

translations.literal: On xinyou day of the fourth month the Hedong floods rose and were about to destroy the walls of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day in the fourth month the Yellow River flooded and threatened Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 帝令決堤岸以分其勢為二河，夾滑城而東，為害滋甚。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the dikes breached to divide its force into two rivers flanking Hua city on the east, and the harm grew worse still.
translations.idiomatic: He breached the dikes to split the flood into two channels east of the city, which only worsened the damage.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝遣許州刺史朱友恭領兵萬人渡淮，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor sent Zhu Yougong, prefect of Xu Prefecture, to lead ten thousand men across the Huai to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: That month he sent Xu Prefect Zhu Yougong with ten thousand men across the Huai with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 時黃、鄂二州累遣使求援，故有是行。

translations.literal: At that time Huang and E prefectures repeatedly sent envoys begging aid, and therefore this expedition was made.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and E prefectures had repeatedly begged for aid, which prompted the expedition.

sentences.zh: 五月，命葛從周統軍屯于洹水，以備蕃軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he ordered Ge Congzhou to command the army encamped at Huanshui to guard against the barbarian forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he stationed Ge Congzhou at Huanshui to block the barbarian army.

sentences.zh: 六月，李克用帥蕃漢諸軍營於斥丘，遣其男落落將鐵林小兒三千騎薄于洹水，從周與戰，大敗之，生擒落落以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Li Keyong led the barbarian and Han armies to camp at Chiqu, sent his son Luoluo to lead three thousand Iron Forest youths in a dash against Huanshui; Congzhou fought them and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Luoluo alive and presenting him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Keyong camped at Chiqu and sent his son Luoluo with three thousand Iron Forest horsemen against Huanshui; Congzhou crushed them and presented Luoluo alive.

sentences.zh: 克用悲駭，請修舊好以贖其子，帝不許，遂執落落送于羅宏信，斬之。

translations.literal: Keyong was grieved and shocked; he requested to renew the old friendship to ransom his son; the Emperor did not consent, and therefore had Luoluo sent to Luo Hongxin and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong, stricken, offered peace to ransom his son; the emperor refused and sent Luoluo to Luo Hongxin, who beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 越七日，我軍還屯陽留以伐鄆。

translations.literal: Seven days later our army returned to camp at Yangliu to attack Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later the army encamped at Yangliu to attack Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，復壁于洹水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again fortified at Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he fortified Huanshui again.

sentences.zh: 是時，昭宗幸華州，遣使就加帝檢校太師，守中書令。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhaozong was at Hua Prefecture and sent envoys to add to the Emperor's titles Acting Grand Preceptor and Guardian of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong, then at Huazhou, promoted him to acting Grand Preceptor and guardian of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，帝以洹水之師大舉伐鄆。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Emperor with the army at Huanshui launched a great campaign against Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he marched from Huanshui in force against Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，營于濟水之次，龐師古令諸將撤木為橋。

translations.literal: On xinmao day he encamped on the bank of the Ji River; Pang Shigu ordered the generals to tear down trees for a bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day he camped on the Ji River; Pang Shigu had his officers build a bridge from felled timber.

sentences.zh: 乙未夜，師古以中軍先濟，聲振於鄆，朱瑄聞之，棄壁夜走。

translations.literal: On the night of yiwei day Shigu with the central army crossed first, and the sound shook Yun; Zhu Xuan heard it and abandoned his walls and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of yiwei, Shigu's center crossed first with a roar that shook Yunzhou; Zhu Xuan abandoned his walls and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 葛從周逐之至中都北，擒瑄並其妻男以獻。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou pursued him to north of Zhongdu, captured Xuan together with his wife and sons, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou pursued him north of Zhongdu, captured Xuan with his wife and sons, and presented them.

sentences.zh: 尋斬汴橋下。

translations.literal: Soon he was beheaded below the Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon beheaded below the Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 鄆州平，乙亥，帝入於鄆，以朱友裕為鄆州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Yun Prefecture was pacified; on yihai day the Emperor entered Yun and made Zhu Youyu military commissioner of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhou fell; on yihai day he entered the city and made Zhu Youyu its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時帝聞朱瑾與史儼兒在豐沛間搜索糧饋，惟留康懷英以守兗州，帝因乘勝遣葛從周以大軍襲兗。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor heard that Zhu Jin and Shi Yan'er were searching for grain and fodder between Feng and Pei, leaving only Kang Huaiying to guard Yan Prefecture; the Emperor therefore seized the victory and sent Ge Congzhou with a great army to strike Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhu Jin and Shi Yan'er were foraging between Feng and Pei while Kang Huaiying held Yanzhou, he sent Ge Congzhou to strike Yan in pursuit of victory.

sentences.zh: 懷英聞鄆失守，俄又我軍大至，乃出降；

translations.literal: Huaiying heard that Yun had fallen, and soon our great army arrived; he then came out to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Huaiying heard Yun had fallen and the main army was upon him; he surrendered;

sentences.zh: 朱瑾、史儼兒遂奔淮南。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin and Shi Yan'er then fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin and Shi Yan'er fled to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 兗、海、沂、密等州平。

translations.literal: Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi were pacified.

sentences.zh: 乃以葛從周為兗州留後。

translations.literal: He then made Ge Congzhou military commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He made Ge Congzhou military commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月丁丑，朱友恭遣使上言，大破淮寇于武昌，收復黃、鄂二州。

translations.literal: On dingchou day of the fifth month Zhu Yougong sent a memorial reporting a great defeat of the Huai bandits at Wuchang and the recovery of Huang and E prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the fifth month Zhu Yougong reported a great victory over the Huai rebels at Wuchang and the recovery of Huang and E.

sentences.zh: 八月，陝州節度使王珙遣使來乞師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wang Gong, military governor of Shan Prefecture, sent envoys to beg troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Gong of Shanzhou begged for troops.

sentences.zh: 是時，珙弟珂實為蒲帥，迭相憤怒，日尋干戈，而珙兵寡，故來求援。

translations.literal: At that time Gong's younger brother Ke was in fact governor of Pu; they mutually raged and daily sought battle; Gong's troops were few, and therefore he came to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's brother Ke held Pu Prefecture; the brothers feuded daily; Gong's forces were few, so he asked for aid.

sentences.zh: 帝遣張存敬、楊師厚等領兵赴陝，既而與蒲人戰於猗氏，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Zhang Cunjing, Yang Shihou, and others to lead troops to Shan; soon they fought the men of Pu at Yishi and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Cunjing and Yang Shihou to Shan; at Yishi they routed the Pu army.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝以兗、鄆既平，將士雄勇，遂大舉南征。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Yan and Yun were already pacified and officers and soldiers were fierce and brave, he then launched a great southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, with Yan and Yun secure and his army eager, he launched a great southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 命龐師古以徐、宿、宋、滑之師直趨清口，葛從周以兗、鄆、曹、濮之眾徑赴安豐。

translations.literal: He ordered Pang Shigu with the armies of Xu, Su, Song, and Hua to press straight on Qingkou, and Ge Congzhou with the masses of Yan, Yun, Cao, and Pu to march directly on Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu was to drive on Qingkou with the armies of Xu, Su, Song, and Hua; Ge Congzhou was to strike Anfeng with the forces of Yan, Yun, Cao, and Pu.

sentences.zh: 淮人遣朱瑾領兵以拒師古，因決水以浸軍，遂為淮人所敗，師古沒焉。

translations.literal: The men of Huai sent Zhu Jin to lead troops to resist Shigu; they therefore breached the water to inundate the army, and so were defeated by the men of Huai; Shigu perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai army sent Zhu Jin against Shigu, breached the dikes to flood his camp, and destroyed him; Shigu died.

sentences.zh: 葛從周行及濠梁，聞師古之敗，亦命班師。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou, marching as far as Haoliang, heard of Shigu's defeat and also ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, reaching Haoliang, heard of Shigu's defeat and ordered a retreat.
